Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Detections and Insights
This workbook template provides an example of how to visualise and gain insights into Microsoft Defender for Office 365.
It allows you to visualise Microsoft Defender for Office 365 (MDO) data based on your organisation needs.
The workbook uses data from hunting tables streamed from Microsoft Defender XDR via the Microsoft Sentinel Connector. Keep the data in the Log Analytics workspace for as long as necessary to get insights over an extended period, based on your organisation's needs.
> **Please note:** *The workbook has a total of 14 tabs. If not all tabs are visible, you can access the remaining tabs using the "..." located at the end of the tab list on the right side.* > --- > **Multi-tenant / multi-workspace:** select one or more workspaces in the **Workspace** filter to view data across them in a single view. For cross-tenant (MSSP) scenarios, onboard customer tenants with **Azure Lighthouse** (their workspaces then appear in the selectors) or use **Microsoft Defender multi-tenant management** in the Defender portal. For performance, keep to ~5–10 workspaces per view.

parameters.name: DefaultWorkspace_Internal
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.operationsmanagement/solutions'
| where name contains 'SecurityInsights'
| project workspaceId = tostring(properties.workspaceResourceId)
| take 1

parameters.name: Subscription
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces'
| distinct subscriptionId, location
| summarize by value = strcat("/subscriptions/", subscriptionId), label = subscriptionId, selected = iff(subscriptionId =~ '{DefaultSubscription_Internal}', true, false)
| order by value asc

parameters.name: Workspace
parameters.query:
resources | where type =~ 'Microsoft.operationsmanagement/solutions' | where name contains 'SecurityInsights' 
| parse name with "SecurityInsights(" label ")" 
| project id = tostring(properties.workspaceResourceId), label, selected = iff(id =~ '{DefaultWorkspace_Internal}', true, false)

Defender for Office 365 - Protection Insights
**Microsoft Defender for Office 365** is a comprehensive security solution designed to protect organizations from advanced threats targeting their email and collaboration tools. It leverages a multi-layered approach to safeguard against phishing, malware, business email compromise (BEC), and other sophisticated attacks.

content.query:
//This query visualises the percentage of emails released from quarantine out of the total ammount of quarantined emails
let Quarantine_Releases = toscalar(EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| where Action == "Quarantine release"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailEvents | where DeliveryLocation == "Quarantine") on NetworkMessageId
| summarize count());
let Quarantined_Mailflow = toscalar(EmailEvents | where DeliveryLocation == "Quarantine"
| summarize count());
print
Quarantine_Releases = toreal(Quarantine_Releases),
Quarantined_Mailflow = toreal(Quarantined_Mailflow),
Release_Percentage = abs(round(((toreal(Quarantine_Releases)/toreal(Quarantined_Mailflow))*100),2))

content.json:
**Effectiveness visually represents the protection given by Defender for Office 365 against phishing and malware in email messages.**
We consider messages that your users report, as well as decisions that are made after delivery.

**Quarantine release rate by detection technology.**
For each detector, the share of its quarantined mail that was later released (Release % = released / quarantined). A high rate can indicate false positives worth reviewing.

content.query:
//Per detection technology: the share of its quarantined emails later released from quarantine (a high rate can indicate false positives). Top 7 by release rate; detectors with <10 quarantined excluded so the rate is meaningful.
EmailEvents
| where DeliveryLocation == "Quarantine"
| extend MDO_detection = parse_json(DetectionMethods)
| extend FirstDetection = iif(isempty(MDO_detection), "Clean", tostring(bag_keys(MDO_detection)[0]))
| extend FirstSubcategory = iif(FirstDetection != "Clean" and array_length(MDO_detection[FirstDetection]) > 0, strcat(FirstDetection, ": ", tostring(MDO_detection[FirstDetection][0])), "No Detection (clean)")
| where FirstSubcategory contains "Malware" or FirstSubcategory contains "Phish"
| join kind=leftouter (
    EmailPostDeliveryEvents
    | where Action == "Quarantine release"
    | distinct NetworkMessageId
    | extend ReleasedFlag = "yes"
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| summarize Quarantined = dcount(NetworkMessageId), Released = dcountif(NetworkMessageId, ReleasedFlag == "yes") by FirstSubcategory
| where Quarantined >= 10 and Released > 0
| extend ReleaseRate = round(Released * 100.0 / Quarantined, 2)
| project ['Detection Technology']=FirstSubcategory, ['Quarantined Emails']=Quarantined, ['Released']=Released, ['Release %']=ReleaseRate
| order by ['Release %'] desc
| take 7

## Most Attacked Users
**The users most targeted by inbound email threats across all threat types (malware, phishing, and spam) in the selected period. Concentrated targeting of a few individuals is a strong signal of deliberate campaigns.**

**Recommended action:** Prioritise these users for security awareness training, tighter protection policies (for example the Strict preset), and closer monitoring - they are your highest-risk people.

content.query:
//This query surfaces the users most targeted by inbound email threats across all threat types (malware, phishing, spam) for the selected period, so SecOps can prioritise the highest-risk individuals. Similar to a "Most Attacked People" view.
EmailEvents
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| where isnotempty(ThreatTypes)
| summarize
    ['Total Threats'] = count(),
    Malware = countif(ThreatTypes has "Malware"),
    Phish   = countif(ThreatTypes has "Phish"),
    Spam    = countif(ThreatTypes has "Spam"),
    ['Last Seen'] = max(Timestamp)
    by ['User']=RecipientEmailAddress
| top 10 by ['Total Threats']
| project ['User'], ['Total Threats'], Malware, Phish, Spam, ['Last Seen']

content.json:
## Detection trend over time - grouped by {Granularity}
**Represents total emails, total detections, total user submissions and admin email submissions over time summarizing the data per {Granularity} interval**

content.query:
//This query visualises total emails, total detections, total user, and admin email submissions over time summarizing the data daily
let gran = {Granularity};
let minTime = toscalar(EmailEvents | summarize min(Timestamp));
let maxTime = toscalar(EmailEvents | summarize max(Timestamp));
let scaffold = range Timestamp from bin(minTime, gran) to bin(maxTime, gran) step gran;
let baseQuery = materialize(EmailEvents
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , "-", RecipientEmailAddress)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| where isnotempty(Timestamp));
let sub = materialize(CloudAppEvents
| extend Record = (parse_json(RawEventData)).RecordType, SubmissionContentType = tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionContentType)
| where Record == 29);
let zapbase = EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , "-", RecipientEmailAddress)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| where ActionResult == "Success"
| where ActionType == "Phish ZAP" or ActionType == "Malware ZAP" or ActionType == "Spam ZAP";
union
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (baseQuery | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Total Inbound Emails"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (baseQuery | where ThreatTypes has ('Phish') | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Emails Detected as Phish"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (baseQuery | where ThreatTypes has ('Malware') | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Emails Detected as Malware"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (baseQuery | where ThreatTypes has ('Spam') | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Emails Detected as Spam"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (baseQuery | where EmailDirection == "Intra-org" | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Total Intra-org Emails"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (baseQuery | where EmailDirection == "Outbound" | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Total Outbound Emails"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (baseQuery | where isnotempty(ThreatTypes) | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Total Emails with Threat"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (sub | where ActionType == "UserSubmission" | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Total Emails Reported by Users"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (zapbase | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Total Emails Removed by ZAP"),
(scaffold | join kind=leftouter (sub | where ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType == "Mail" | summarize Count = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran)) on Timestamp | project Timestamp, Count = coalesce(Count, 0), Details = "Total Emails Reported by Admins")

content.json:
## Bad traffic (%) - Inbound Emails - grouped by {Granularity}
**This represents bad traffic (% of emails with threats) compared to total inbound emails, summarized per {Granularity} interval over time.**

content.query:
//This query visualises bad traffic (% of emails with threats) compared to total inbound emails over time summarising the data daily.
EmailEvents
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| summarize TotalEmailCount = count(),
            BadEmailCount = countif(isnotempty(ThreatTypes)) by bin(Timestamp, {Granularity})
| extend Bad_Traffic_Percentage_Inbound = todouble(round(BadEmailCount / todouble(TotalEmailCount) * 100, 2))
| project Timestamp, ['Bad Traffic %'] = Bad_Traffic_Percentage_Inbound

# Malware detection insights

---

This tab provides insights into email message **detections** by Microsoft Defender for Office 365 where the message contained a **malware threat** (such as viruses, spyware, or ransomware) within its **URLs** or **attachments**.

Malware Detection Trends, Threat Classes, and Malware Names
This section consolidates key visuals that track and explain malware detections in inbound email as identified by Microsoft Defender for Office 365 focusing on per-{Granularity} trend, threat classes and Malware types.

**Recommended action:** If malware volume spikes, confirm Safe Attachments (Block mode) is enabled for all users and investigate the top malware families below.

### Malware Detection Trend
**This visual displays a per-{Granularity} trend of email malware detections identified by Microsoft Defender for Office 365. The area chart summarises the number of messages flagged for malware threats.**

content.query:
//This query visualises total emails with Malware detections over time summarizing the data daily.
let gran = {Granularity};
let agg = materialize(EmailEvents 
| where ThreatTypes has "Malware" 
| where OrgLevelPolicy != "Phishing simulation" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox"
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , "-", RecipientEmailAddress) 
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| summarize MalwareDetections = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran));
range Timestamp from toscalar(agg | summarize min(Timestamp)) to toscalar(agg | summarize max(Timestamp)) step gran
| join kind=leftouter (agg) on Timestamp
| project Timestamp, MalwareDetections = coalesce(MalwareDetections, 0)
| sort by Timestamp asc

content.json:
### Malware Detection Trend - Advanced Threats
**Not all threats are going to be easily recognisable, that's why Microsoft Defender for Office 365 has advanced threat detection methods, that use virtual sandbox environments to detonate URLs and Files. These virtual sandbox technologies look for known patterns, such as a recognisable login page in a URL, or a file accessing command and control infrastructure. This visual displays a per-{Granularity} trend of Malware detections of these advanced threats**

content.query:
//This query visualises total emails with Malware detections over time summarizing the data daily by Malware detection technologies/controls used for detecting unknown-unique malware.
let gran = {Granularity};
let agg = materialize(EmailEvents
| where DetectionMethods has 'Malware'
| where OrgLevelPolicy != "Phishing simulation" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox"
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , '-', RecipientEmailAddress) 
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| extend ParsedMethods = parse_json(DetectionMethods)
| mv-expand MalwareMethod = ParsedMethods.Malware
| where MalwareMethod in ('File detonation','URL detonation')
| summarize Count = count() by MalwareMethod = tostring(MalwareMethod), Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran));
range Timestamp from toscalar(agg | summarize min(Timestamp)) to toscalar(agg | summarize max(Timestamp)) step gran
| extend d = 1 | join kind=inner (agg | distinct MalwareMethod | extend d = 1) on d | project Timestamp, MalwareMethod
| join kind=leftouter (agg) on Timestamp, MalwareMethod
| project Timestamp, MalwareMethod, Count = coalesce(Count, 0)
| sort by MalwareMethod asc, Timestamp asc

content.query:

EmailEvents 
| where OrgLevelPolicy != "Phishing simulation" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox"

| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , "-", RecipientEmailAddress) 
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key

EmailEvents

| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , "-", RecipientEmailAddress) 
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key

| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key

| summarize Count = count() by ThreatName

| project ['Threat Name'] = ThreatName, Count

This section consolidates key visuals that track and explain malware detections delivery locations, detection technologies used for detections, sender infrastructure insights in inbound email identified by Microsoft Defender for Office 365 as Malware.

### Malware Detections by SenderIPv4 Geo Location
**Visualizes the email sending infrastructure sender IPv4 addresses associated with inbound emails detected as Malware, along with the IPv4 address geographic coordinates (latitude, longitude) and country information. Helps identify high-risk regions and sources for targeted threat mitigation.**

content.query:
//This query visualises total emails with Malware detections summarizing the data by email sender IP address (SenderIPv4).
EmailEvents 
| where ThreatTypes has 'Malware' and isnotempty(SenderIPv4)
| where OrgLevelPolicy != "Phishing simulation" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox"
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , '-', RecipientEmailAddress) 
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| summarize count() by SenderIPv4
| extend GeoInfo = geo_info_from_ip_address(SenderIPv4)
| extend Latitude = tostring(GeoInfo.latitude), Longitude = tostring(GeoInfo.longitude)
| project SenderIPv4, Latitude, Longitude, count_

**Not all threats are easily recognizable, which is why Microsoft Defender for Office 365 uses advanced detection methods, including virtual sandbox environments to detonate URLs and files. **Microsoft Defender for Office 365 uses Language AI for Phish and Business Email Compromise (BEC) detection. Teams Calls and Vishing (Voice Phishing)
**Voice phishing (vishing) over Microsoft Teams is the fastest-growing collaboration threat of 2026. Attackers impersonate IT help desk or support and call users directly, often after a chat lure, to talk them into granting remote access or entering credentials. Because a target must be online to answer, malicious calls cluster in working hours. This section surfaces Teams call activity, when calls happen, and callers using support or brand-impersonation identities.**

*Interim data source: Teams call activity is currently read from Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps call telemetry (CloudAppEvents). It will move to the dedicated CallActivityEvents table once that table is available to stream into Microsoft Sentinel.*

**Recommended action:** Treat unsolicited help desk or support calls as suspicious. Confirm any request through a known internal channel, and never grant remote access such as Quick Assist on the strength of an inbound Teams call. Restrict inbound calls and chat from unmanaged and consumer tenants.

### Teams call activity over time
**Distinct Microsoft Teams calls per selected interval. A sudden rise, or calls outside normal working hours, can indicate a vishing campaign in progress.**

content.query:
//Distinct Teams calls per interval (interim source: CloudAppEvents / CallParticipantDetail).
CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "CallParticipantDetail"
| extend R = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend CallId = tostring(R.CallId)
| summarize ['Teams Calls'] = dcount(CallId) by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, {Granularity})
| sort by Timestamp asc

content.json:
### When calls happen (hour of day, UTC)
**Microsoft Teams calls by the hour of day they started (UTC), listed 00:00 through 23:00. The bar length is the number of calls that started in that hour across the selected period. Vishing calls cluster in working hours because the target must be online to answer, with the heaviest malicious-call activity between 14:00 and 20:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, according to Microsoft Threat Intelligence. Use this to baseline normal call timing and spot unusual off-hours spikes.**

content.query:
//Teams calls by start hour of day (UTC), all 24 hours 00:00..23:00 in order (interim source: CloudAppEvents / CallParticipantDetail).
let data = CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "CallParticipantDetail"
| extend R = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend JoinTime = todatetime(R.JoinTime), CallId = tostring(R.CallId)
| where isnotempty(JoinTime) and isnotempty(CallId)
| summarize CallStart = min(JoinTime) by CallId
| extend HourUTC = hourofday(CallStart)
| summarize Calls = count() by HourUTC;
range HourUTC from 0 to 23 step 1
| join kind=leftouter (data) on HourUTC
| extend Calls = coalesce(Calls, 0)
| extend HourLabel = strcat(iif(HourUTC < 10, strcat("0", tostring(HourUTC)), tostring(HourUTC)), ":00")
| order by HourUTC asc
| project ['Hour of Day (UTC)'] = HourLabel, ['Teams Calls'] = Calls

content.json:
### Suspicious callers (support and helpdesk impersonation)
**Teams call participants whose display name or address looks like IT support, help desk, or a well-known brand (for example "Microsoft IT support", "Help Desk", "Office 365 Support"), or who dial in from a throwaway `.onmicrosoft.com` tenant. Origin shows whether the caller is external, an external throwaway tenant, or inside your own tenant. External and throwaway-tenant callers are the primary vishing risk; own-tenant matches are frequently a legitimate internal help desk and should be confirmed rather than assumed malicious.**

**Recommended action:** Prioritise External and `.onmicrosoft` callers, confirm none are legitimate, and warn the users they called. Genuine IT support does not cold-call staff over Teams to request remote access.

content.query:
//Suspicious Teams callers by impersonation-style DISPLAY NAME or address (Attendees[].DisplayName / UPN), with Origin from the org's own accepted (EmailEvents inbound) domains - no tenant-id anchor. Interim source: CloudAppEvents / CallParticipantDetail.
let suspRegex = @"(?i)help ?desk|helpdesk|it ?support|service ?desk|sys ?admin|administrator|security|microsoft|google|apple|amazon|paypal|support|update|verif|account|password|mfa|maintenance";
let ownDomains = toscalar(EmailEvents | where EmailDirection == "Inbound" | extend RD = tolower(tostring(split(RecipientEmailAddress, "@")[1])) | where isnotempty(RD) | summarize make_set(RD, 200));
let calls = CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "CallParticipantDetail"
| extend R = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend CallId = tostring(R.CallId), JoinTime = todatetime(R.JoinTime), Attendees = R.Attendees
| where isnotempty(CallId);
let callAtt = calls | summarize Attendees = take_any(Attendees), JoinTime = min(JoinTime) by CallId;
callAtt
| mv-expand Att = Attendees
| extend Caller = tolower(tostring(Att.UPN)), CallerName = tostring(Att.DisplayName)
| extend CallerDom = tostring(split(Caller, "@")[1])
| where isnotempty(Caller)
| extend SuspName = CallerName matches regex suspRegex or Caller matches regex suspRegex
| where SuspName or CallerDom endswith ".onmicrosoft.com"
| extend Origin = case(CallerDom endswith ".onmicrosoft.com", "External (.onmicrosoft throwaway)", set_has_element(ownDomains, CallerDom), "Own tenant", "External")
| summarize CallsPlaced = dcount(CallId), FirstSeen = min(JoinTime), LastSeen = max(JoinTime) by CallerName, Caller, Origin
| extend OriginRank = case(Origin == "External (.onmicrosoft throwaway)", 0, Origin == "External", 1, 2)
| sort by OriginRank asc, CallsPlaced desc
| take 10
| project ['Caller Display Name'] = CallerName, ['Caller Address'] = Caller, ['Origin'] = Origin, ['Calls Placed'] = CallsPlaced, ['First Seen'] = FirstSeen, ['Last Seen'] = LastSeen

Teams Impersonation & Identity Deception
Microsoft Defender for Office 365 flags Teams messages where a sender impersonates a brand, a specific person, or a trusted domain. Impersonation is the entry point for most Teams social-engineering: attackers pose as IT, executives, or Microsoft to build trust before delivering a malicious link or request. content.query:

MessageEvents
| where IsExternalThread == true
| extend SenderDomain = tolower(tostring(split(SenderEmailAddress, "@")[1]))

| extend ThreatPct = round(todouble(ThreatMessages) * 100 / TeamsMessages, 1)
| project ['Sender Display Name']=SenderDisplayName, ['Sender Address']=SenderEmailAddress, ['Why Flagged']=WhyFlagged, ['Teams Messages']=TeamsMessages, ['Threat Messages']=ThreatMessages, ['Threat %']=ThreatPct, ['First Seen']=FirstSeen, ['Last Seen']=LastSeen

Teams Message and Call Submissions
Microsoft Teams messages and calls reported by users, and messages submitted by admins, for review by Microsoft. Sourced from the submission records in CloudAppEvents.

**Recommended action:** Encourage users to report suspicious Teams messages and calls so Microsoft can tune protection, and triage admin submissions promptly. A cluster of reports naming the same sender, display name, or call identity is an early signal of a targeted campaign: pivot those identities into the impersonation and risky-sender views above to scope it.

content.query:
//This query summarizes Microsoft Teams message and call submissions reported to Microsoft for the selected period, split by user and admin reports. Only completed submissions are counted (submission triage/timeout lifecycle records are excluded).
let sub = materialize(CloudAppEvents
| extend RD = parse_json(RawEventData)
| extend RecordType = tostring(RD.RecordType), SubmissionContentType = tostring(RD.SubmissionContentType)
| where RecordType == "29" and SubmissionContentType in ("ChatMessage", "TeamsCall"));
union
(sub | where SubmissionContentType == "ChatMessage" and ActionType == "UserSubmission" | summarize Count = count() | extend Details = "Messages Reported by Users", Ord = 1),
(sub | where SubmissionContentType == "TeamsCall" and ActionType == "UserSubmission" | summarize Count = count() | extend Details = "Calls Reported by Users", Ord = 2),
(sub | where SubmissionContentType == "ChatMessage" and ActionType == "AdminSubmission" | summarize Count = count() | extend Details = "Messages Submitted by Admins", Ord = 3)

This section provides key visuals that highlight top attacked users – individuals most frequently targeted by inbound email threats as detected by Microsoft Defender for Office 365. **Recommended action:** Apply the Strict preset to the most-attacked users and review the top sender domains as possible block-list candidates.

**Displays the top 10 recipient email addresses that received inbound emails flagged as Spam, Phishing, or Malware. Helps identify high-risk users for targeted security awareness and policy enforcement.**

content.query:
// This query visualises the top 10 users that are receiving Spam, Phishing or Malware emails
EmailEvents 
| where  OrgLevelPolicy != "Phishing simulation" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox" and EmailDirection =="Inbound"
| extend MDO_detection = parse_json(DetectionMethods) 
| extend FirstDetection = iif(isempty(MDO_detection), "Clean", tostring(bag_keys(MDO_detection)[0]))

| extend ThreatEmailCount=(MalwareEmailCount+PhishEmailCount+SpamEmailCount)
| extend Bad_Traffic_Percentage_Inbound = todouble(round(ThreatEmailCount / todouble(TotalEmailCount) *100, 2))
| top 15 by ThreatEmailCount
| project ['Recipient']=RecipientEmailAddress, ['Total Emails']=TotalEmailCount, ['Threat Emails']=ThreatEmailCount, ['Malware']=MalwareEmailCount, ['Phish']=PhishEmailCount, ['Spam']=SpamEmailCount, ['Bad Traffic %']=Bad_Traffic_Percentage_Inbound

Automatic External Email Forwarding Insights
**Email forwarding can be useful, but can also pose a security risk due to the potential disclosure of information.**
Users can configure [Inbox rules](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/Outlook/mail/use-rules-to-automatically-forward-messages) in Outlook or set up [SMTP forwarding](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/turn-on-automatic-forwarding-in-outlook-7f2670a1-7fff-4475-8a3c-5822d63b0c8e) to automatically forward messages to external recipients. You can control automatic external email forwarding from cloud mailboxes using [Outbound spam policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/outbound-spam-policies-external-email-forwarding) in Microsoft Defender for Office 365. **Attackers might exploit this capability to compromise your organization or its partners.**

**Recommended action:** Investigate external auto-forwarding - it is a common data-exfiltration path. Consider disabling auto-forwarding via the outbound spam policy unless a business case is documented.

# Email detection action overrides --- This tab provides insights into admin or end-user configured **detection overrides** where the message was detected as a threat by Microsoft Defender for Office 365, however an admin-configured policy or end-user setting overrode the detection action.[

Learn more

](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/step-by-step-guides/understand-overrides-in-email-entity)

Admin configured Detection Overrides (Allow)
This section consolidates key visuals that track emails subject to administrator policies (e.g., Transport Rules, Tenant Allow/Block List) with an "Allow" action, overriding Microsoft Defender for Office 365 detections (excluding SecOps Mailbox overrides).

**Recommended action:** Review Allow overrides that later carried threats and remove stale or overly broad allow entries - they weaken protection.

### Admin Overrides (Allow) Trend
**Displays the count (per {Granularity}) of emails where an administrator policy with an "Allow" action overrode detections (excluding SecOps Mailbox). Helps track the frequency of admin overrides over time.**

content.query:
//This query visualises the ammount of emails subject to an admin policy with action of allow independent of action taken, summarizing the data daily
let gran = {Granularity};
let agg = materialize(EmailEvents
| where isnotempty(OrgLevelPolicy) and OrgLevelPolicy!="SecOps Mailbox" and OrgLevelAction == "Allow"
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , '-', RecipientEmailAddress) 
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| summarize TotalAdminOverrides = count() by Timestamp = bin(Timestamp, gran));
range Timestamp from toscalar(agg | summarize min(Timestamp)) to toscalar(agg | summarize max(Timestamp)) step gran
| join kind=leftouter (agg) on Timestamp
| project Timestamp, ['Admin Overrides'] = coalesce(TotalAdminOverrides, 0)
| sort by Timestamp asc

User & Sender Override Detail (Allow)
Inbound messages that Microsoft Defender for Office 365 **detected as threats but delivered anyway** because of an admin- or user-configured **Allow** override (phishing-simulation and SecOps Mailbox traffic excluded). **Total Threats** is all detected threats to that recipient / sender domain in the selected range; **Overridden Threats** and **Override %** are the portion delivered due to an Allow override, and **Override Types** names the specific overrides responsible. **User-configured** overrides come from the recipient's own mailbox junk-email settings in Outlook / Outlook on the web (the mailbox "safelist collection") — the **Safe Senders** and **Safe Recipients** lists and **trusted contacts** ("Also trust email from my Contacts"). **Admin-configured** overrides come from the **Tenant Allow/Block List, Exchange mail flow (transport) rules, the IP Allow List, or allowed sender/domain lists in anti-spam policies**. Use this to spot users or domains where overrides are letting threats through — candidates for policy review or a Tenant Allow/Block List (TABL) block.

**Recommended action:** Focus on the users and sender domains with the most allow overrides - these are the biggest protection gaps.

content.query:
//Top recipients receiving threats that were delivered due to an admin or user override, with the share of their threats that were overridden and a breakdown of which override types caused them.
EmailEvents
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and isnotempty(ThreatTypes) and OrgLevelPolicy != "Phishing simulation" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox"
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId, "-", RecipientEmailAddress)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| extend OverrideType = case(
    OrgLevelAction == "Allow" and OrgLevelPolicy != "" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox", OrgLevelPolicy,
    UserLevelAction == "Allow", strcat("User: ", UserLevelPolicy),
    "(none)")
| summarize PerType = count() by RecipientEmailAddress, OverrideType
| summarize TotalThreats = sum(PerType),
            OverriddenThreats = sumif(PerType, OverrideType != "(none)"),
            OverrideTypes = strcat_array(make_set_if(strcat(OverrideType, " (", PerType, ")"), OverrideType != "(none)"), "; ")
        by RecipientEmailAddress
| where OverriddenThreats > 0
| extend OverridePercent = round(OverriddenThreats * 100.0 / TotalThreats, 1)
| top 15 by OverriddenThreats
| project ['Recipient']=RecipientEmailAddress, ['Total Threats']=TotalThreats, ['Overridden Threats']=OverriddenThreats, ['Override %']=OverridePercent, ['Override Types']=OverrideTypes

//Top sender domains sending threats to users, with the share of those threats that were delivered because of an admin or user override and a breakdown of which override types caused them. High override rates are strong candidates for policy review or a Tenant Allow/Block List (TABL) block.
EmailEvents
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound" and isnotempty(ThreatTypes) and OrgLevelPolicy != "Phishing simulation" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox"
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId, "-", RecipientEmailAddress)
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| extend OverrideType = case(
    OrgLevelAction == "Allow" and OrgLevelPolicy != "" and OrgLevelPolicy != "SecOps Mailbox", OrgLevelPolicy,
    UserLevelAction == "Allow", strcat("User: ", UserLevelPolicy),
    "(none)")
| summarize PerType = count() by SenderFromDomain, OverrideType
| summarize TotalThreats = sum(PerType),
            OverriddenThreats = sumif(PerType, OverrideType != "(none)"),
            OverrideTypes = strcat_array(make_set_if(strcat(OverrideType, " (", PerType, ")"), OverrideType != "(none)"), "; ")
        by SenderFromDomain
| where OverriddenThreats > 0
| extend OverridePercent = round(OverriddenThreats * 100.0 / TotalThreats, 1)
| top 10 by OverriddenThreats
| project ['Sender Domain']=SenderFromDomain, ['Total Threats']=TotalThreats, ['Overridden Threats']=OverriddenThreats, ['Override %']=OverridePercent, ['Override Types']=OverrideTypes

# False Negative(FN) Submissions insights

---

This tab provides insights into email message **False Negative(FN) Submissions** performed by users or administrators in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 where the message reported to have **Malware, Phish or Spam threat** within its **content, URLs or attachments**.

False Negative(FN) Admin submissions
This section provides insights into email message **False Negative(FN) Submissions performed by administrators** in Microsoft Defender for Office 365 where the message reported to have Malware, Phish or Spam threat within its content, URLs or attachments.

**Recommended action:** Prioritise admin-submitted misses for policy tuning; recurring sender domains may be block-list candidates.

### False Negative(FN) Admin Submissions per-{Granularity} trend by submission types 
**Displays counts (per {Granularity}) of False Negative(FN) Admin Submissions grouped by submission type (Spam, Phish, Malware) and content type (Mail, URL, Attachment). Helps to monitor where detections were missed and later submitted by admins as false negatives to Microsoft.**

### False Negative(FN) Admin Submissions by submission types 
**Displays counts (per {Granularity}) of False Negative(FN) Admin Submissions grouped by submission type (Spam, Phish, Malware) and content type (Mail, URL, Attachment).**

### False Negative(FN) Admin Submissions by submission State
**Displays the total count of False Negative(FN) Admin Submissions by submission State (e.g., Pending, Completed, Failed). Helps track the processing status of admin submissions and identify bottlenecks or errors.**

content.query:
//This query visualises the total ammount of admin false negative submission by submission type.
CloudAppEvents 
| where ActionType contains "Submission"
| extend SubmissionType = tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionType),SubmissionContentType=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionContentType)
| extend Admin_SubmissionType=
iff(SubmissionType == "2" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="Mail","Malware (Mail)",
iff(SubmissionType == "1" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="Mail","Phish (Mail)",
iff(SubmissionType == "0" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="Mail","Spam (Mail)",
iff(SubmissionType == "2" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="URL","Malware (URL)",
iff(SubmissionType == "2" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="Attachment","Malware (Attachment)",
iff(SubmissionType == "1" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="URL","Phish (URL)",
iff(SubmissionType == "1" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="Attachment","Phish (Attachment)",
"Other")))))))
| where Admin_SubmissionType!="Other"
| summarize count() by Admin_SubmissionType

//This query visualises the total ammount of admin false negative submissions by the state of the submission.
CloudAppEvents 
| where ActionType contains "AdminSubmission" 
| extend Record = (parse_json(RawEventData)).RecordType,SubmissionState = parse_json(RawEventData).SubmissionState,SubmissionId=parse_json(RawEventData).SubmissionId,SubmissionType = parse_json(RawEventData).SubmissionType,SubmissionContentType=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionContentType)
| where Record == 29 and SubmissionType in ("0","1","2")
| summarize count() by tostring(SubmissionState)

content.json:
### False Negative(FN)/False Positive(FP) Admin Submissions by Triage Verdict
**Displays the total count of False Negative(FN)/False Positive(FP) Admin Submissions grouped by TriageVerdict (e.g., Malware, Spam, Phish, Clean). Helps assess how submissions were graded during triage and identify detection gaps.**

### Top Admins Submitting False Negatives 
**Displays the top 15 admin accounts that submitted the highest number of false negative messages (missed detections) via AdminSubmission. Helps identify key contributors to threat remediation and potential patterns in detection gaps.**

content.query:
//This query visualises the total ammount of admin false negative or false positive submissions by the verdict of the submission grading.
CloudAppEvents 
| where ActionType contains "AdminSubmissionTriage" 
| extend UserKey = (parse_json(RawEventData)).UserKey, SubmissionState = (parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionState,  SubmissionId=(parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionId, TriageVerdict=(parse_json(RawEventData)).GradingResult.TriageVerdict 
| summarize count() by tostring(TriageVerdict)

//This query visualises the top admins performing false negative submissions
CloudAppEvents 
| where ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" 
| extend Record= (parse_json(RawEventData)).RecordType,SubmissionState = (parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionState, UserId = (parse_json(RawEventData)).UserId,SubmissionType = parse_json(RawEventData).SubmissionType  
| where Record == 29 and SubmissionType in ("0","1","2")
| summarize ['Submissions']=count() by ['Admin']=tostring(UserId)
| top 15 by ['Submissions'] desc

content.json:
### False Negative(FN) Admin Submissions by Top Sender Domains
**For each top sender domain that admins reported missed threats for, shows the domain's MDO-detected threat profile (emails with threats and the Malware/Phish/Spam breakdown), the count of admin FN submissions, and the submission rate (Admin Submission % = admin submissions / total inbound from the domain). A high rate can flag a domain whose mail is frequently reported as missed.**

content.query:
//Top 10 sender domains that admins reported false negatives (missed threats) for, with each domain's MDO-detected threat profile for context.
let subs = CloudAppEvents
| where ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted"
| extend SubmissionType = tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionType), SubmissionContentType=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionContentType), P2SenderDomain=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).P2SenderDomain)
| where SubmissionContentType == "Mail" and SubmissionType in ("2","1","0")
| summarize AdminSubmissions=count() by P2SenderDomain;
let domainProfile = EmailEvents
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| summarize TotalInbound=count(), EmailsWithThreats=countif(isnotempty(ThreatTypes)), Malware=countif(ThreatTypes has "Malware"), Phish=countif(ThreatTypes has "Phish"), Spam=countif(ThreatTypes has "Spam") by SenderFromDomain;
subs
| join kind=leftouter (domainProfile) on $left.P2SenderDomain == $right.SenderFromDomain
| extend AdminSubmissionPct = round(AdminSubmissions * 100.0 / todouble(coalesce(TotalInbound, AdminSubmissions)), 2)
| top 10 by AdminSubmissions desc
| project ['Sender Domain']=P2SenderDomain, ['Emails With Threats']=coalesce(EmailsWithThreats,0), ['Malware']=coalesce(Malware,0), ['Phish']=coalesce(Phish,0), ['Spam']=coalesce(Spam,0), ['Admin Submissions']=AdminSubmissions, ['Admin Submission %']=AdminSubmissionPct

content.json:
### False Negative(FN) Admin Submissions by admin Detection override types
**Displays the top 10 cases where emails were submitted as false negatives by admins, even though they were initially detected by Microsoft Defender for Office 365 but delivered due to an admin policy override. Includes details on PolicyOverride, PolicySource, and DetectionVerdict for deeper insight into override behaviour.**

content.query:
//This query visualises emails submitted as false negatives by admins where emails where already detected by MDO but there was a admin policy override
CloudAppEvents 
| where ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" 
| extend SubmissionType = tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionType),SubmissionContentType=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).SubmissionContentType)
| extend Admin_SubmissionType=
iff(SubmissionType == "2" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="Mail","Malware (Mail)",
iff(SubmissionType == "1" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="Mail","Phish (Mail)",
iff(SubmissionType == "0" and ActionType == "AdminSubmissionSubmitted" and SubmissionContentType=="Mail","Spam (Mail)","Other"))),
P2SenderDomain=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).P2SenderDomain),NetworkMessageId=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData).ObjectId)),DetectionVerdict=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).DeliveryMessageInfo.FinalFilterVerdict),PolicyOverride=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).DeliveryMessageInfo.PolicyOverride),PolicyPolicyOverrideType=tostring((parse_json(RawEventData)).DeliveryMessageInfo.PolicySource)
| where SubmissionContentType == "Mail" and SubmissionType in ("2","1","0") and PolicyOverride !="NoOverride"
| summarize count() by PolicyOverride, PolicyPolicyOverrideType,DetectionVerdict,Admin_SubmissionType
| top 10 by count_ desc
| project ['Policy Override']=PolicyOverride, ['Override Source']=PolicyPolicyOverrideType, ['Detection Verdict']=DetectionVerdict, ['Submission Type']=Admin_SubmissionType, ['Emails']=count_

### False Negative(FN) User Submissions of already detected Emails (from Junk folder)
**Displays the total count of False Negative(FN) User Submissions where the email message was already detected by Microsoft Defender for Office 365 and the detection action was configured to deliver the message into the Junk folder of the user mailbox. It breaks down the result based on the original detection verdict determined by Microsoft Defender for Office 365. Helps track the user submissions of messages that already had a detection. Consider changing the detection action to Quarantine to avoid these submissions.**

content.query:
//This query visualises the total ammount of user false negative submissions that are already detected by MDO and already delivered in the junk folder

# Post-Delivery & Quarantine Insights

---
This tab covers what happens to threats **after delivery**: Zero-hour Auto Purge (ZAP) remediation of malicious messages already in mailboxes, and quarantine management - what is held, released, and by whom. Together they show how effectively post-delivery response contains threats that reached the inbox.

Post Delivery Protection offered by ZAP
This section provides insights into Microsoft Defender for Office 365's post-delivery protection capabilities through Zero-Hour Auto Purge (ZAP). ZAP is a critical security feature that continuously monitors delivered emails and automatically removes messages that are later identified as malicious. These visuals help track ZAP effectiveness, response times, and remediation patterns.

**Recommended action:** High post-delivery ZAP volume means threats are reaching inboxes before being caught - review pre-delivery filtering and detection latency.

### ZAP Post-Delivery Actions (per {Granularity})
**Shows the count (per {Granularity}) of emails that were remediated post-delivery by Zero-Hour Auto Purge (ZAP). Helps track how often threats are detected and removed after reaching user mailboxes.**

### ZAP Actions by Detection Type (per {Granularity})
**Visualizes the count (per {Granularity}) of post-delivery remediation actions performed by Zero-Hour Auto Purge (ZAP), broken down by detection type (Spam ZAP, Phish ZAP, Malware ZAP). Helps track which threat categories are most frequently remediated after delivery.**

### ZAP Remediation by Destination
**This visual shows where ZAP moves malicious emails during remediation. Post-delivery actions can send emails to different locations: Quarantine (isolated for admin review), Deleted Items (soft delete), Junk Email folder, or back to Inbox (for false positive corrections). Understanding these patterns helps evaluate ZAP policy configurations and ensures malicious content is properly isolated from users.**

Quarantine Management and Insights
This section provides comprehensive insights into quarantine operations, including release patterns, detection methods, and threat categorization. It helps security teams understand what types of threats are being quarantined and monitor quarantine release activity to identify potential false positives or security policy effectiveness.

**Recommended action:** Investigate high release rates - they indicate false positives or risky user releases; review quarantine policies and release permissions.

### Quarantine Release Trend
**This visual displays the per-{Granularity} trend of emails released from quarantine by administrators. Monitoring this metric helps identify patterns in quarantine management and potential areas where policy adjustments may be needed to reduce unnecessary quarantines.**

### Quarantine Release Percentage
**Calculates the percentage of quarantined emails that were successfully released compared to the total quarantined messages. This metric helps measure engagement with quarantine and assess the effectiveness of quarantine policies.**

### Quarantine Release Analysis by Detection Type
**For each detection technology, this shows the share of its quarantined emails that were later released from quarantine (Release % = released / quarantined). A high release rate flags a detector that may be over-flagging legitimate mail - a strong candidate for policy or rule tuning. The Released count shows the volume behind each rate.**

content.query:
//This query visualises the percentage of emails released from quarantine out of the total ammount of quarantined emails
let Quarantine_Releases = toscalar(EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| where Action == "Quarantine release"
| join kind=leftouter (EmailEvents | where DeliveryLocation == "Quarantine") on NetworkMessageId
| summarize count());
let Quarantined_Mailflow = toscalar(EmailEvents | where DeliveryLocation == "Quarantine"
| summarize count());
print
Quarantine_Releases = toreal(Quarantine_Releases),
Quarantined_Mailflow = toreal(Quarantined_Mailflow),
Release_Percentage = abs(round(((toreal(Quarantine_Releases)/toreal(Quarantined_Mailflow))*100),2))

//Per detection technology: the share of its quarantined emails that were later released from quarantine.
//Release % = released / quarantined for that detection technology - a high rate flags a detector that may be over-flagging legitimate mail (potential false positives). Detectors with fewer than 10 quarantined emails are excluded so the rate is statistically meaningful.
EmailEvents
| where DeliveryLocation == "Quarantine"
| extend MDO_detection = parse_json(DetectionMethods)
| extend FirstDetection = iif(isempty(MDO_detection), "Clean", tostring(bag_keys(MDO_detection)[0]))
| extend FirstSubcategory = iif(FirstDetection != "Clean" and array_length(MDO_detection[FirstDetection]) > 0, strcat(FirstDetection, ": ", tostring(MDO_detection[FirstDetection][0])), "No Detection (clean)")
| where FirstSubcategory contains "Malware" or FirstSubcategory contains "Phish" or FirstSubcategory contains "Spam"
| join kind=leftouter (
    EmailPostDeliveryEvents
    | where Action == "Quarantine release"
    | distinct NetworkMessageId
    | extend ReleasedFlag = "yes"
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| summarize Quarantined = dcount(NetworkMessageId), Released = dcountif(NetworkMessageId, ReleasedFlag == "yes") by FirstSubcategory
| where Quarantined >= 10 and Released > 0
| extend ReleaseRate = round(Released * 100.0 / Quarantined, 2)
| project ['Detection Type']=FirstSubcategory, ['Quarantined Emails']=Quarantined, ['Released']=Released, ['Release %']=ReleaseRate
| order by ['Release %'] desc

This tab provides a view for security operations. Combines incident response metrics with investigation insights to evaluate the effectiveness of both automated systems and manual interventions.

Security Incident Response Metrics
**Operational efficiency insights.** Tracks incident volume, resolution speed, automation efficacy, and classification accuracy to evaluate SOC performance.

**Recommended action:** Track mean time to close by severity against your SLA and investigate any severity trending upward.

### Email Security Incidents
**These visuals display the per-{Granularity} trend of email-related security incidents, as well as the proportion of email incidents compared to the total number of incidents in Defender.**

content.query:
// Filter for incidents that have at least one Email Security alert
let gran = {Granularity};
let OfficeEmailAlerts = SecurityAlert
    | where ProductName contains "Office 365 Advanced Threat Protection" or ProductName contains "Microsoft 365 Defender"
    | project SystemAlertId;
let agg = materialize(SecurityIncident
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| mv-expand AlertIds
| where isnotempty(AlertIds) and not(Title startswith "CC_")
| extend AlertId = tostring(AlertIds) 
| join kind=inner
    (OfficeEmailAlerts | extend SystemAlertId = tostring(SystemAlertId))
    on $left.AlertId == $right.SystemAlertId
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *), AlertCount = dcount(AlertId) by IncidentNumber
| summarize Incidents_Number = count() by TimeGenerated = bin(TimeGenerated, gran));
range TimeGenerated from toscalar(agg | summarize min(TimeGenerated)) to toscalar(agg | summarize max(TimeGenerated)) step gran
| join kind=leftouter (agg) on TimeGenerated
| project TimeGenerated, ['Email Security Incidents'] = coalesce(Incidents_Number, 0)
| sort by TimeGenerated asc

// Categorize incidents: Email Security vs Other
let AllAlerts = SecurityAlert
    | extend SystemAlertId = tostring(SystemAlertId)
    | project SystemAlertId, ProductName;
SecurityIncident
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by IncidentNumber
| mv-expand AlertIds
| where isnotempty(AlertIds) and not(Title startswith "CC_")
| extend AlertId = tostring(AlertIds)
| join kind=inner
    (AllAlerts)
    on $left.AlertId == $right.SystemAlertId
| summarize AlertSystems = make_set(ProductName) by IncidentNumber
| extend HasEmailSecurity = 
    AlertSystems has "Office 365 Advanced Threat Protection" or

### Average Incident Time To Close (minutes)
**This visual displays the average time, in minutes, to close email-related security incidents (per {Granularity}), split by severity, so you can see how resolution speed changes over time. Reference SLA targets: High 60, Medium 120, Low 240, Informational 480 minutes.**

content.query:
// SLA thresholds by severity for email-security (MDO) incidents
let SLA_Variables = datatable (Severity:string, TimeToResolve:int) [
    "High", 60,
    "Medium", 120,
    "Low", 240,
    "Informational", 480
];

// Identify MDO-related incidents via alert correlation
let EmailSecurityIncidents = 
    SecurityIncident
    | mv-expand AlertIds
    | where isnotempty(AlertIds)
    | extend AlertId = tostring(AlertIds)
    | join kind=inner (
        SecurityAlert
        | where ProductName in ("Office 365 Advanced Threat Protection", "Microsoft 365 Defender")
        | extend AlertId = tostring(SystemAlertId)
        | project AlertId
    ) on AlertId
    | distinct ProviderIncidentId;

// Get latest incident state for each MDO-related incident
let LatestMdoIncidents =
    SecurityIncident
    | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, Classification, Status, Severity, CreatedTime, ClosedTime, Title) by ProviderIncidentId
    | where ProviderIncidentId in (EmailSecurityIncidents)
    | where not(Title startswith "CC_");  // Exclude non-email incidents as needed

LatestMdoIncidents
| where Status == "Closed"
| extend TimeToResolveIncident = datetime_diff('minute', ClosedTime, CreatedTime)
| join kind=inner SLA_Variables on Severity
| summarize
    ['Avg Time to Close (min)'] = avg(TimeToResolveIncident),
    CountIncidents = count(), Breached = countif(TimeToResolveIncident > TimeToResolve)
    by Day = bin(ClosedTime, 1d), Severity
| order by Day asc, Severity asc

// AIR investigation outcomes by day: ThreatDetected vs. Clean

// Step 1: Deduplicate automated remediation events by message and recipient
let AutoRemediations = 
    EmailPostDeliveryEvents
    | where ActionType == "Automated Remediation"
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, ActionResult) by NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress, Timestamp;

// Step 2: Derive threat verdicts using AlertEvidence
let EvidenceVerdicts =
    AlertEvidence
    | where EntityType in ("MailMessage", "MailCluster")
    | extend extra = todynamic(AdditionalFields)
    // If this is a mail cluster, use provided NetworkMessageIds array; otherwise wrap NetworkMessageId as a single-item array
    | extend networkIds = iff(
      isnull(extra.NetworkMessageIds) or array_length(extra.NetworkMessageIds) == 0,
      pack_array(NetworkMessageId),          // create a single-element array using pack_array
      extra.NetworkMessageIds                // use the array as-is if it exists
    )
    | mv-expand nmID = networkIds                // expand to individual message IDs
    // Derive verdict from LastVerdict, ThreatAnalysisSummary, and ThreatIntelligence
    | extend 
        lastVerdict = tolower(tostring(extra.LastVerdict)),
        threatAIList = extra.ThreatAnalysisSummary,
        threatInt   = extra.ThreatIntelligence
    | extend verdictFromAnalysis = iff(array_length(threatAIList) > 0, tolower(tostring(threatAIList[0].Verdict)), ""),
             verdictTI          = iff(array_length(threatInt) > 0, "malicious", "")   // any item in ThreatIntelligence indicates malicious
    // Mark as threat-detected if verdict is malicious/suspicious or threat evidence is present
    | extend ThreatDetectedFlag = 
        case(
            lastVerdict in ("malicious","suspicious") or verdictFromAnalysis in ("malicious","suspicious")
                or verdictTI == "malicious",
            true,
            false
        )
    // Weight mail clusters by MailCount; default to 1 for single messages
    | extend MailCountInt = toint(extra.MailCount)
    | extend Weight = iff(EntityType == "MailCluster", 
                        coalesce(MailCountInt, 1), // default to 1 if MailCount is missing
                        1)
    | summarize IsThreatDetected = any(ThreatDetectedFlag), 
                WeightSum       = sum(Weight) 
    by nmID = tostring(nmID);

// Step 3: Join remediation events with verdicts and aggregate by day
AutoRemediations
| join kind=leftouter EvidenceVerdicts on $left.NetworkMessageId == $right.nmID
| extend isThreat      = coalesce(IsThreatDetected, false), 
         effectiveWeight= coalesce(WeightSum, 1)
| extend InvestigationOutcome = iif(isThreat, "Threat Detected", "Clean")
| summarize PreventionCount = sum(effectiveWeight) by Day = bin(Timestamp, {Granularity}), InvestigationOutcome
| order by Day asc, InvestigationOutcome asc

//This query shows if the action taken after an Automated Investigation required manual approval by and admin or was automatically taken
EmailPostDeliveryEvents
| extend Key = strcat(NetworkMessageId , '-', RecipientEmailAddress) 
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by Key
| where ActionType == "Automated Remediation"
| summarize count() by ActionTrigger
